subject: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - benchmark harness & next steps
messages:
From: Priya Suresh <priya.s@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeFin Eng Team <eng@edgefin.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - next steps

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the call today - that was really helpful. Quick recap + asks so we can get the benchmark run scheduled: 

Summary of EdgeFin targets (high-level):
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for single-request generation (non-streaming) at 1024 tokens.
- Streaming: token-level streaming (SSE) must start delivering first token within 80ms and sustain steady stream without dropped chunks.
- Throughput: baseline goal 2M tokens/minute across our staging cluster (roughly ~500 tokens/sec sustained per instance under expected concurrency).
- Concurrency: sustain 250 concurrent active requests with <15% tail amplification on p95.

What we need from Redwood to validate:
1) Benchmark methodology doc + eval harness you mentioned (prompt sets, seed/repro rules, measurement definitions).
2) Sample prompt set and payload formats so our infra team can prep staging load.
3) Recommended run config (instance types, quantization flags, warmup iterations, KV-cache settings).

I attached our current SLO spreadsheet (edgefin-slos.xlsx) with more details.

Next steps: can you send the harness and proposed measurement definitions? We'd like to run an initial smoke run in staging the week of Nov 30.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Suresh
Head of Platform, EdgeFin

--
Attachment: edgefin-slos.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Suresh <priya.s@edgefin.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T17:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - next steps

Hi Priya - great to connect this morning. Thanks for the clear targets.

Attaching a first-pass benchmark harness bundle and our methodology doc: benchmark-methodology.md and redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.zip. The harness includes:
- a runner that can operate in both closed-loop (fixed concurrency) and open-loop (poisson arrival) modes,
- streaming client for token-by-token SSE measurement,
- measurement scripts for p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, throughput counters, and token-level delivery timing.

Key measurement definitions we'll use (short):
- Latency (non-streaming): time from request accepted by service to final token emitted (end-to-end); report p50/p95/p99.
- Streaming latency: time to first token (TTFT) and median inter-token interval; we'll report TTFT p50/p95.
- Throughput: tokens/sec sustained over a 5-minute window after warmup; warmup = 3 minutes or 500 requests, whichever is longer.
- Concurrency profile: measured as active in-flight requests; we recommend closed-loop runs at 50/100/200/250 to see scaling.
- Reproducibility: deterministic prompt seeds where applicable; we'll record RNG seeds and model/config checksums and publish run metadata (Dockerfile + image digest).

Questions/notes for you:
- Can you confirm SSE streaming semantics (chunk sizes, any framing) and whether you need server-side chunk batching?
- For throughput targets, do you mean aggregate across the staging cluster (we'll need instance counts) or per-instance sustained tokens/sec?

Propose: Redwood runs an initial harness in our dedicated test fleet and shares the raw run artifacts; EdgeFin runs the same harness in staging and we compare. If that works, we can schedule smoke on Nov 30.

Thanks - sending attachments now.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.zip (archive, ~4MB), benchmark-methodology.md (text, 7KB)

From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.s@edgefin.com>, EdgeFin Eng Team <eng@edgefin.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - next steps

Thanks Marissa - a few clarifications from the eng side after reviewing the doc: 

1) Streaming: yes, SSE token-by-token is required. We typically expect the first token within ~80ms for short prompts; for longer context the TTFT can be up to 120ms but sustained inter-token latency must stay <= 50ms median. We do not want server-side micro-batching for streaming responses unless it can guarantee those bounds.

2) Concurrency/throughput: our staging cluster for the test will have 12 instances (mX.large equivalent). Our aggregate goal is ~2M tokens/minute - that maps to ~166k tokens/min per instance (~2770 tokens/sec) - which is higher than Marissa's note. Apologies for the earlier estimate; we need the harness to show both per-instance and aggregate numbers.

3) Model/config reproducibility: we use a quantized model build (int8) in staging; can Redwood run the same quantized variant? If not, we need comparative numbers vs float32 baseline. Also please capture kernel/runtime params (CUDA/cuDNN/driver) in run metadata.

4) Prompt set: we'll attach a representative sample (edgefin-sample-prompts.json). Prompts include short transactional queries (15-40 tokens) and longer summarization prompts (~800-1,024 tokens). We care most about p95 on short queries and streaming TTFT on long replies.

Can you confirm you can run with quantized weight files and report both per-instance and aggregate throughput? Also can you share the harness run command we should use to replicate locally?

Thanks,
Amit
Senior SRE, EdgeFin

--
(attachment: edgefin-sample-prompts.json)

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@edgefin.com>, Priya Suresh <priya.s@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - next steps

Hi Amit / Priya - Dev from the Redwood infra team here. Quick notes on the harness and reproducibility: 

- The harness (https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks) supports running with both float32 and quantized models (we have an int8 quant path). We can accept model blobs or pull from an S3-compatible staging bucket; recommend supplying the quantized artifacts (weights + config) so we run identically.
- Repro: harness records Docker image digest, model sha256, runtime libs (CUDA + driver versions) and the seed file used for any non-deterministic ops. We also output a compressed artifact of raw timings + traces for independent analysis.
- Run command (example): 
  ./run_benchmark --mode closed-loop --concurrency 250 --duration 600 --model s3://edgefin/staging/model-int8.tar.gz --prompts edgefin-sample-prompts.json --streaming sse --output runs/edgefin-20261130

- For streaming we have a streaming client that measures TTFT and inter-token deltas; it supports optional server-side batching flags but will default to per-token flush to match your TTFT constraints.

If you can provide the quantized model tarball and confirm the instance type (mX.large equiv) we'll stage a run on our cluster and share the raw artifacts. Also: do you want us to run both closed-loop and open-loop modes? We recommend both to understand amplification.

Thanks - Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Inference
Redwood Inference

--
Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks

Thanks Dev - this looks good. We've attached the prompt sample and will share the quantized model tarball via a staging S3 link by EOD Friday (Nov 27).

EdgeFin ask for the run:
- Please run both closed-loop at concurrency = [50, 100, 200, 250] and open-loop with target arrival rates matching 50%, 75%, and 100% of our expected aggregate throughput.
- Include both int8 and float32 runs if possible, so we can compare latency/throughput tradeoffs.
- Deliverables: raw timing artifacts, aggregated CSVs (p50/p90/p95/p99), streaming TTFT histogram, and a short results note.

We will provision staging credentials (S3 URL + temp keys) and share a short Runbook in the Drive link.

Thanks - Priya

Great - thanks everyone. A few final coordination items before we lock the smoke run for Nov 30: 

1) Schedule: Redwood will run an initial int8 + float32 sweep on Nov 30 (08:00 - 12:00 PST) against our dedicated test fleet and post raw artifacts to the Drive folder. EdgeFin will run the same harness in staging the week of Dec 1 and we'll compare.

2) Access: Priya - please send the S3 link + temp creds and the Drive Runbook. We'll request minimal IAM access (read-only for model blob, write for results).

3) Repro/metadata: Dev - please ensure the run artifact includes Docker image digest, model sha256, runtime libs, and the prompt seed file.

4) Acceptance criteria: Priya / Amit - can you confirm the acceptance criteria we should gate on after the run? My suggestion: p95 (non-streaming) <= 300ms at concurrency 250 for short prompts OR streaming TTFT p95 <= 120ms for long prompts, and aggregate throughput within 10% of your target. If that sounds good we'll mark that as the success criteria for the smoke.

5) NDA/Legal: If required for access to model artifacts we can run under our standard mutual non-disclosure; let me know and I'll have our legal team loop in.

If there are no objections I'll schedule the run and share invites + the Drive link.

Thanks - looking forward to this.

Best,
Marissa Cole
